..
The trade-wind regime will continue for the Marianas, promoting
periods of isolated showers with limited convection due to a 
temperature inversion and drier mid-level air stifling vertical 
growth. There may be potential for a brief period of low-end scattered
showers on Friday, but deterministic and ensemble accumulated 
precipitation are leaning towards isolated. According to the U.S. 
Drought Monitor, there is no indication of drought occurring in the
Marianas. However, little to no rainfall over the past several weeks
should not be overlooked as total rainfall amounts at this time of 
year are about 3 inches below normal. As such, water conservation 
efforts are encouraged as dry season approaches, which could 
potentially introduce abnormally dry (D0) conditions across the 
region.

Marine...
Gentle to moderate northeasterlies will continue through the forecast
period. Combined seas of 5 to 6 feet are comprised of a dominant 
trade swell and a secondary northwest swell. Beginning Friday, seas 
will increase to 6 to 8 feet as an elevated, long-period north swell
from distant Typhoon Cempaka approaches the region, in addition to 
the prevailing trade swell. At the same time, surf along north-facing
reefs may become hazardous, leading to dangerous swimming conditions
and a high risk of rip currents. For now, a headline was included 
several days in advance to communicate such hazard.

Eastern Micronesia...
The Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) blankets a good portion of eastern
Micronesia with spotty showers and isolated thunderstorms in the 
vicinity of the NET this afternoon. The NET is expected to continue 
to weaken throughout the next couple of days. Isolated to low-end 
scattered showers are expected to prevail throughout the forecast 
period at all forecast sites; though, some higher-end scattered 
showers will be possible tonight through Friday night at Majuro as an
approaching trough moves through the RMI. Isolated thunderstorms 
will also be possible Thursday and Friday at Majuro.

Light to gentle north to northeast winds at Pohnpei and Kosrae will 
become more easterly on Thursday and persist through the weekend. 
Light to gentle easterly winds will persist through much of Friday at
Majuro and become more north to northeast starting Friday night, 
then becoming variable late on Saturday. Combined seas of 4 to 6 feet
will generally prevail at all forecast points with seas consisting 
of a northeast, a north-northwest, and a small, southeast swell.

Most of Eastern Micronesia is experiencing abnormally dry (D0) drought
conditions. Try to start conserving water as we are transitioning 
into the dry season. 

Western Micronesia...
An area of convergence is over Palau and Yap. This is forecast to 
bring scattered showers to these islands. However, model guidance 
suggests these showers have about 2 inches of Precipitable WATer 
(PWAT) to pull from. This could lead to quick burst of showers, while
the rest of the day remain dry. While these showers may bring some 
temporary drought relief, Palau being in a moderate drought (D1) and 
Yap being in abnormally dry (D0), these categories are not expected 
to change this week. Overall, intermittent light to moderate 
scattered showers are expected through the beginning of next week. 
Try to start conserving water as we are transitioning into the dry 
season.

For Chuuk, a ridge of high pressure has built in and will inhibit 
shower development through at least the beginning of next week. Chuuk
remains abnormally dry (D1 drought category) for this time of year. 
Try to start conserving water as we are transitioning into the dry 
season.

As for marine conditions near Palau and Yap, seas of 5 to 6 feet 
will gradually build over the next several days as a swell from 
distant Typhoon Cempaka will enter Palau and Yap's coastal waters 
later this week. This swell will bring heightened seas and elevated 
surf along north facing reefs. Surf levels are forecast to approach 
the thresholds of High Surf Advisory of 9 feet, however, at this time
surf is not anticipated to breach that threshold. Conditions near 
Chuuk are forecasted to remain around 5 to 6 feet through the 
forecast period. East to north winds across the region will be light 
to moderate.
